acceptance: morize-core exports BoundedVec, CollectionBoundsError, BoundedVecBuildError, and BoundedVecPushError from one new bounded-collection module, with no additional domain behavior.
BoundedVec::<u8, 2> accepts empty, one-item, and two-item vectors while over-limit Vec construction fails with max_items=2 and actual_items=3 and returns the original Vec unchanged and in order.
MAX_ITEMS=0 accepts only an empty collection; failed construction and failed push return rejected data without mutating, truncating, reordering, or dropping it.
try_push succeeds below capacity and, at capacity, leaves the existing collection unchanged while BoundedVecPushError returns the exact rejected value and bounded AtCapacity metadata.
as_slice and into_vec preserve element order and values exactly; equality, ordering, and hashing follow the underlying ordered values without hidden normalization.
Debug for BoundedVec, BoundedVecBuildError, and BoundedVecPushError reports bounded metadata only and does not format or expose contained/rejected T values.
The public API exposes no mutable Vec reference and implements no DerefMut, AsMut<Vec<T>>, IndexMut, unchecked push/extend/insert, or equivalent bound-bypass surface.
cargo fmt --all -- --check passes on the exact implementation head.
cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline passes on the exact implementation head.
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --offline -- -D warnings passes on the exact implementation head.
cargo test --workspace --all-targets --offline passes and includes focused boundary, lossless rejection, preservation, value-semantics, and Debug non-disclosure tests.
Cargo manifests and Cargo.lock are unchanged; the Grain admits no runtime, build, or test dependency.
GitHub Actions passes Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows on the exact implementation head before acceptance.

An independent semantic reviewer reviews the exact implementation head for boundary correctness, lossless rejection, order/value preservation, no-bypass API surface, Debug non-disclosure, scope containment, and required evidence.
ADR-0004 proof prerequisite for SG-000011 revalidates against the exact WorkPacket baseline before execution.
The implementation changes no path outside crates/morize-core/src/bounded_collection.rs and crates/morize-core/src/lib.rs.

method.control: Implementation is limited to one dependency-free bounded ordered collection module, focused tests, and morize-core re-exports. No field-specific limits, maps/sets, serialization, persistence, domain records, or third-party dependencies are authorized.
method.review_separation: An independent semantic reviewer must review the exact implementation head, item-count boundaries, lossless rejection, no-bypass API surface, Debug non-disclosure, and required evidence separately from the implementing agent before acceptance.
method.rollback: Revert the bounded ordered collection implementation commits; no persisted format, migration, or user data depends on this Grain.

minimality.rationale: A single standard-library-only ordered collection wrapper inside existing morize-core is the narrowest reusable bounded-collection contract. Returning rejected values avoids hidden data loss while keeping field limits, serialization, maps/sets, and domain policy out of scope.

outcome: morize-core exposes a dependency-free BoundedVec<T, const MAX_ITEMS: usize> ordered collection that enforces a hard item-count ceiling, preserves order and values, returns rejected data on failed construction or push, and exposes no mutation path that can bypass the bound.
rationale: P1 explicitly requires bounded collections and the data-model contract requires bounded field sizes. This Grain adds only a reusable in-memory ordered collection primitive; field-specific limits, maps/sets, serialization, persistence, domain records, and collection policy remain separate decisions.

risk.recovery: Revert the bounded ordered collection implementation commits; no persistent format or user data has been written by this Grain.

scope_in: Define public BoundedVec<T, const MAX_ITEMS: usize> with private Vec<T> storage and an exact item-count ceiling.
Define bounded metadata-only CollectionBoundsError plus lossless BoundedVecBuildError<T> and BoundedVecPushError<T> wrappers that return rejected values without exposing their contents through Debug.

Provide empty construction, checked Vec<T> construction, lossless try_push, as_slice, len, is_empty, into_vec, max_items, AsRef<[T]>, and deterministic Clone/Eq/Ord/Hash value semantics where T supports them.
Keep all mutating storage private: do not expose DerefMut, AsMut<Vec<T>>, IndexMut, mutable Vec access, unchecked push/extend/insert, or any other API that can exceed MAX_ITEMS.

Add standard-library-only tests for zero limits, exact boundaries, over-limit construction, lossless failed construction, lossless failed push, stable order/value preservation, value semantics, and Debug non-disclosure.
scope_out: Field-specific aliases or maximums, unordered maps/sets, uniqueness/deduplication, sorting, normalization, pagination, concurrency, domain-specific collection semantics, or automatic truncation.
Serde or other serialization-framework integration, persisted schemas, configuration formats, wire contracts, migrations, storage, retrieval, policy, MCP, models, or domain records.
Any third-party runtime, build, or test dependency.
